lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Opens with her saying she already understood you, setting the secret tenderness of the first letters.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Her vivid account of Flush throwing himself on her after the frightening church escape.

lines.text: But if one heart and one life will do, ... they are yours ...
lines.note: Her promise that one heart and one life are yours, a central early vow.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Her private joke that she is your Flush and he is hers, turning the dog-stealer debate into shared language.

lines.text: Now it is changed ... the feeling is—and I am not afraid even so—except sometimes of losing your affection by some fault of my own—I am not afraid that it would be a fault of yours, remember.
lines.note: Her admission that she is only afraid of losing your affection, showing the depth of her trust.

lines.text: And smiling to myself I was, both last night and this morning, at your phrase about the ‘business’ to be talked by the ‘grave man and woman’; understanding your precaution against all unlawful jesting!—jesters forbidden in the protocol!
lines.note: Her smile at your phrase about the grave man and woman talking business, a private joke about the marriage plans.

lines.text: I look back, and in every one point, every word and gesture, every letter, every silence—you have been entirely perfect to me—I would not change one word, one look.
lines.note: Your declaration that you would not change one word or look of hers, a sweeping backward look of love.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: Her gratitude that all she is, she owes to you, a strong thank-you from the wedding aftermath.

lines.text: I have a right now openly to love you, and to hear other people call it a duty, when I do, ... knowing that if it were a sin, it would be done equally.
lines.note: Her joy at being able to love you openly after the secret wedding.

lines.text: You know what I would have done to possess you:—now that I do possess you, I renew the offer to you ... judge with what earnest purpose of keeping my word!
lines.note: Your promise that now you possess her, you renew the offer to possess you, sealing the new relation.

lines.text: And then ... imagine the comfort I take to the deepest of my heart from these hands held out to me!
lines.note: Her comfort in the hands held out to her by your family, a grateful acceptance of your world.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Her refusal to leave your letters behind, however heavy the ounces, a final keepsake of the courtship.
